# Add or Change a State Reducer

## Context
Reducers are pure value types in `src/ConsoleForge/Core/`. A model stores the reducer (or the widget's plain fields) and the widget's `Update` rebuilds a reducer, applies the key, and copies the result back. Entry points: [`TextInputState.HandleKey()`](mex://method:c4876d4b7b071801c973889bd8d0a9ff) (single line, grapheme-aware), [`TextAreaState.HandleKey()`](mex://method:91ea3d89e7b70002bdb96fd1c2cd93f8) (only what crosses lines; single-line edits delegate to `TextInputState`), [`ListState.HandleKey()`](mex://method:9a282d316364347caed946814804b389) (selection + scroll over a *count*, not items).

## Steps
1. Put the rule in the reducer, not the widget. New operations are public methods returning a new instance (`MoveTo`, `DeleteWordBackward`, `WithViewport`).
2. Return **the same instance** when the key does nothing — widgets use `ReferenceEquals(after, before)` to return `this`, which keeps the model reference unchanged and skips a redraw.
3. Normalise invariants in one private place (`Normalize`, `ListState.EnsureVisible`) so every constructor and operation clamps the same way.
4. Map keys in `HandleKey`; bind printable characters by character, and keep Ctrl chords consistent across reducers (`Ctrl+A`/`Ctrl+E`, `Ctrl+U`/`Ctrl+K`, `Ctrl+W`, `Ctrl+←/→`).
5. Make the widget delegate (see `TextInput.Update`); if a widget already had its own copy of the rule, delete it.
6. Test in `tests/ConsoleForge.Tests/Core/{Name}StateTests.cs`; the widget test only asserts delegation.

## Gotchas
- Cursor positions are indices into the string but must move by grapheme cluster (`StringInfo`), never by UTF-16 unit — an emoji must not split.
- `ListState` holds `Count`, not items, so it serves filtered views and virtualised pages; scroll is maintained on every move only if `ViewportHeight` is set. `List` currently constructs it without a viewport, and there is no way to learn the real viewport from layout yet (WISHLIST item 9) — consumers pass it in.
- Adding a binding to a reducer changes every widget that delegates to it — mention it in `CHANGELOG.md` under Changed.

## Verify
- Reducer tests cover: no-op returns same instance, boundaries (start/end, empty), grapheme clusters, and each new binding.
- `dotnet test tests/ConsoleForge.Tests --filter "FullyQualifiedName~StateTests"` then the full suite.
- Public members documented; `CHANGELOG.md` updated.

## Debug
- Key does nothing: check `KeyMsg.Key` vs `KeyMsg.KeyChar` and modifiers — `AnsiTerminal` decodes Ctrl+letter as a control character.
- Widget and model disagree: find a second copy of the rule outside the reducer.
